Audit logs format, retention and export
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira Patel: okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is Samira from Redwood, I have Ethan and Lucia with me. we slotted 45 to 60 mins, hope that's still good.
[00:00:12] Mark Delaney: yep, thanks Samira, we have about 50 minutes, priyas on the call and jamie and alex are here as well. goal is to validate the compliance artifacts and figure out the RBAC/SSO flows before wrapping procurement.
[00:00:29] Ethan Park: great, I'll do a quick screen share of the Trust Center — but first quick agenda, SOC2 artifacts, ISO scoping, roles & SSO, audit logs and KMS. sound okay?
[00:00:41] Priya Sharma: yes, perfect. quick note, we are strict on data residency — any customer data must stay in eu-west-1 for now.
[00:00:50] Lucia Gomez: noted, we'll flag region pinning options.
[00:00:58] Speaker 3: (mumble) there was a question on retention earlier —
[00:01:05] Samira Patel: sorry who's that? I think that's Alex.
[00:01:07] Alex Ruiz: yeah sorry, my line was muted. procurement just wants to be clear on how long logs are retained and whether we can export them for our audit.
[00:01:18] Ethan Park: totally. on the Trust Center we have the SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate and a controls-mapping spreadsheet that shows how Redwood controls map to SOC/ISO criteria, i'll pull that up.
[00:01:33] Samira Patel: quick caveat — some customer-specific evidence is under the dedicated/private flow; we keep operational logs in the audit-exports, but redact PII unless specifically requested with a valid SIR.
[00:01:48] Mark Delaney: when you say dedicated/private, do you mean Dedicated clusters or the Private VPC offering?
[00:01:54] Ethan Park: good Q — Dedicated is our reserved capacity offering managed by Redwood, Private is customer-controlled VPC + option for on-prem bundle. for compliance customers often ask for Private because they want control over networking and KMS.
[00:02:07] Priya Sharma: about KMS — can you describe the HSM support? we need customer-managed keys, and FIPS 140-2 compatibility.
[00:02:16] Lucia Gomez: yes. Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS apis — we also support bring-your-own-HSM for the on-prem package. Ethan, do you want to add more technical?
[00:02:29] Ethan Park: sure. we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault for hosted; for BYOK we provide key-wrapping and local HSM chaining. FIPS note: the HSM vendor and config matter, but we can provide guidance and run an integration test.
[00:02:46] Mark Delaney: okay, that's promising. and audit logs — format, retention and can we pull raw events into our SIEM?
[00:02:55] Ethan Park: audit logs are JSON-line events with timestamps, actor, action, resource and request-id. default retention is 90 days in hosted, longer for Dedicated (configurable) and Private you manage retention. We provide a streaming export to S3 or to syslog/HTTP sink — customers often pipe to Splunk or SumoLogic.
[00:03:16] Jamie O'Neill: any PII redaction on the logs? we need to ensure subject identifiers are hashed.
[00:03:22] Samira Patel: by default we do minimal redaction; we redact tokens and secrets. for hashed identifiers we can work with you to implement a transform in the export pipeline.
[00:03:33] Priya Sharma: on control mapping — do you map each Redwood control to SOC2 CC criteria and ISO Annex A? we need a matrix for our auditors.
[00:03:42] Lucia Gomez: yes, the matrix maps to SOC 2 CC and ISO 27001 Annex A controls, and we annotate evidence artifacts (policy docs, architecture diagrams, test results). we'll share the spreadsheet.
[00:03:54] Alex Ruiz: can we get a read-only link to the artifacts? procurement would prefer to view before we sign.
[00:04:02] Samira Patel: absolutely. i'll send a Trust Center link and create a short-lived read-only token. noted as action item.
[00:04:08] --- (screen share starts) ---
[00:04:20] Ethan Park: opening the controls sheet — you can see rows for control id, description, mapped SOC control, mapped ISO control, artifact link, last updated. some artifacts are internal (redacted) — those will show as summary notes.
[00:04:40] Priya Sharma: hmm i see a gap around key rotation evidence — do you have key rotation logs in the evidence set?
[00:04:46] Ethan Park: good catch. rotation evidence for hosted KMS is in the key-management logs; we can pull those for you but some entries show service-level ops events that we summarize. we'll add a redwood-managed key-rotation report.
[00:04:58] Mark Delaney: what about SSO — SAML is mandatory for us and SCIM provisioning. can you map roles in RBAC to our internal roles?
[00:05:08] Lucia Gomez: yes we have an RBAC template — it supports role hierarchies and custom roles. SCIM provisioning is supported to create users and map groups. We usually recommend an admin role, infra role, app-developer role with least privilege.
[00:05:21] Priya Sharma: do you support attribute-based access control? we use department=trading to gate certain datasets.
[00:05:28] Ethan Park: A-BAC is not first-class today; we can approximate with group-based RBAC attributes and custom claims in SAML. if ABAC is a hard requirement, we can capture that in the POC scope.
[00:05:39] Alex Ruiz: procurement question: if we go Dedicated, does Redwood still hold any keys?
[00:05:45] Samira Patel: for Dedicated — Redwood manages the nodes but you can opt into customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. only Private with BYOK and HSM means Redwood does not have access to unwrapped keys.
[00:05:58] Mark Delaney: sounds like Private is preferable then. what is the uplift and timeline?
[00:06:04] Lucia Gomez: uplift depends on sizing and whether you want on-prem. typical timeline for Private VPC setup is 4–8 weeks after contract; on-prem adds more time. we'll put together an estimate.
[00:06:18] --- [00:06:30] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) ---
[00:06:35] Ethan Park: quick note on attestation scope: our SOC 2 Type II covers the hosted API control environment; some controls for Dedicated/Private are customer-controlled and thus have a different evidence set. we clearly annotate that in the mapping.
[00:06:52] Priya Sharma: auditors will expect to see evidence for patch management and vuln scanning — do you have scan reports?
[00:06:59] Ethan Park: yes, we have weekly vulnerability scan summaries and monthly penetration test executive summaries. full pen test reports are controlled; we can provide redacted findings and remediation timelines.
[00:07:12] Mark Delaney: data residency — can we force requests to be served from a single region for EU customers?
[00:07:19] Samira Patel: yes, we have routing policies that can pin requests to region; for strict residency we recommend Private with egress control. for hosted, we provide region preference but not strict physical isolation unless Dedicated/Private is selected.
[00:07:34] Jamie O'Neill: about logging latency — how soon do logs appear? near real-time?
[00:07:40] Ethan Park: typically within 30 seconds to a minute for the audit stream. there can be spikes during incident windows. for high-throughput customers we suggest streaming exports to your S3/siem so you don't wait for in-console ingestion.
[00:07:56] Priya Sharma: can you demonstrate an example export?
[00:08:01] Ethan Park: yes i'll demo a small JSON export — bear with a sec. 
[00:08:10] --- (short pause, demo noise) ---
[00:08:28] Ethan Park: here's a sample event: { timestamp, request_id, user_id, action, resource, status, meta }. you'll get more fields in the real export.
[00:08:41] Mark Delaney: okay that looks fine. we'll need a SHA256 of user identifiers and a flag for PII masking.
[00:08:49] Samira Patel: we can add a transform step before the export to hash identifiers. that's a typical pattern.
[00:08:55] Alex Ruiz: procurement — any third party subprocessor list? we need it for our vendor review.
[00:09:02] Lucia Gomez: yes, we'll add the subprocessors list to the Trust Center. it includes cloud providers and monitoring vendors. some entries are covered by DPAs.
[00:09:12] Priya Sharma: one more on ISO — our audit needs proof of ISMS controls and statements of applicability. do you provide SoA?
[00:09:21] Ethan Park: we provide a high-level SoA and policies mapped to Annex A. for Redwood Private, you may need to supplement with your own ISMS evidence.
[00:09:32] Mark Delaney: outstanding item: control gap around key rotation and ABAC. can we capture these as POC scope?
[00:09:40] Samira Patel: yes — we'll add ABAC evaluation and key rotation evidence collection to the POC scope.
[00:09:46] --- [00:10:00 to 00:30:00 omitted] ---
[00:30:12] Priya Sharma: quick interruption — we need to align on retention numbers: 7 years for certain logs is a hard regulatory ask for us, can Redwood keep 7 years in a dedicated customer bucket?
[00:30:24] Ethan Park: 7 years is long but doable in Dedicated or Private; for hosted retention beyond 1 year we typically put logs in long-term S3 archive with associated costs. we'll send a cost estimate.
[00:30:38] Mark Delaney: cost estimate please.
[00:30:40] Samira Patel: noted. action item: cost for 7-year retention in Dedicated vs Private.
[00:30:48] Jamie O'Neill: on encryption in transit — TLS ciphers? do you enforce minimum TLS 1.2? we require TLS 1.3 where possible.
[00:30:57] Ethan Park: we support TLS 1.2 and 1.3; default is 1.2+ but we can enforce 1.3 in your environment.
[00:31:05] Priya Sharma: do you have SOC 2 bridge letters for customers that need interim attestation?
[00:31:11] Lucia Gomez: yes, we can provide a bridge letter and statement of scope for the current audit period.
[00:31:17] Alex Ruiz: timeline: when can we expect the Trust Center link and reports?
[00:31:22] Samira Patel: i'll share the link and SOC 2 by end of day Friday (2026-12-10).
[00:31:29] Mark Delaney: excellent. next, scheduling the KMS deep dive — who should attend from Redwood?
[00:31:36] Samira Patel: Ethan + our platform security engineer and Lucia for compliance context. we'll coordinate dates.
[00:31:44] Priya Sharma: for the POC — can we get a short term Dedicated environment with BYOK for the test?
[00:31:52] Ethan Park: yes we can provision a small Dedicated pool for evaluation; we'll include KV cache config to mimic your latency profile.
[00:31:59] Mark Delaney: perfect. procurement will open a PO after we review the Trust Center.
[00:32:05] --- wrap-up ---
[00:32:10] Samira Patel: recap: I'll send Trust Center link + SOC 2 Type II, Lucia will add RBAC mapping template, Ethan will share audit log sample & KMS integration notes, Priya will send mandatory controls list. we'll schedule KMS deep dive and provide cost for 7-year retention.
[00:32:28] Priya Sharma: thanks — i'll also circulate our auditor contact if you need to sync.
[00:32:33] Alex Ruiz: procurement expects redlined contract attached to the Trust Center artifacts?
[00:32:38] Samira Patel: we can attach contract language examples and a subprocessors list.
[00:32:45] Mark Delaney: anything else?
[00:32:49] Lucia Gomez: nothing from us. thanks all.
[00:32:52] Samira Patel: thanks everyone, will follow up with artifacts and calendar invites. bye.
[00:33:00] (call ends)
notes: Transcription has occasional mislabels and missing utterances; some demo audio overlap. Customer emphasized residency and KMS BYOK. Agreed POC scope includes ABAC evaluation and key rotation evidence collection.
